q: What is an ACMA and what does the role do?
a: The Acquisition Career Management Advocate — a command-nominated, DACM-chartered senior leader (GO/SES/GS-15/colonel level) who serves as the strategic advisor for acquisition career development: advises leadership on DAWIA certification and career development, keeps the organization informed on certification status, and designates the Lead Organizational Point of Contact (OAP). Chartered up to four years, renewable. Full role explainer: ACMA Resource Center.

q: What is the departure notification clause and why does it matter?
a: A clause on Acquisition & Contracting: advance notice of departing contractor personnel so access is revoked cleanly — accounts disabled on departure, tokens collected, artifacts and knowledge transferred. It matters because orphaned accounts are a top audit finding and lost knowledge transfer leaves systems fragile. Pair it with the Personnel Access Standards clause for full lifecycle coverage.

q: What is an IDP and do I need one?
